alignments.note: זָהָב rendered *golden splendor*, headed on the word carrying the lexeme, since *splendor* alone is any splendor (rule 31); the marginal *Hebrew gold* corroborates and decides nothing (rule 38).

The ASV realizes this one noun twice, as the fronted subject *God* and the resumptive *him* of *upon him*, so both belong to its one discontinuous unit, headed on the first occurrence (rule 25). The competing reading gives *God* to the noun and leaves *him* unlicensed, which would make a written pronoun `added` while the morpheme it realizes held only half the ASV's English.

Supplied possessive verb. Rule 43 counts the clause's English words against the morphemes that could carry them: `עַל` has already been spent on the written *upon*, and a preposition on which the ASV has spent its own word stands in the same position as an absent one, so it is not what makes the clause possessive and is not a home for a second English word. No `הָיָה`, no suffix, no verb and no noun of possession stands in the clause, so nothing is left for the *hath* to complete and it is its own `added` unit under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, exactly as rule 43 leaves the *hath* of `אוֹ תְבַלֻּל בְּעֵינוֹ` and the *shall have* of `יוֹסֵף חֲבָלִים`. The competing reading, which the accepted alignment took, gives *hath upon* to `עַל` under rule 43's earlier sentences and heads it on *upon*; but those sentences govern a preposition that is itself the predicate and for which the ASV writes no preposition at all, as `לָהֶם מִסְגְּרוֹת` → *they had panels* and `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* are, and rule 49 sends a written *have* to rule 43 rather than keeping it with the preposition.
עַל rendered *upon*, the word written for its own relation (rule 11).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied *hath* was moved out of the `עַל` unit and marked `added`. `עַל` already holds the written *upon*, so under rule 43's counting paragraph it is not a home for a second English word, and no other morpheme in the clause makes it possessive.
The double realization of `אֱלוֹהַּ` as *God ... him* is retained under rule 25 and the alternative is named in that unit's note (rule 8).
The marginal *Hebrew gold* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
